text:
maria: quick brain dump — proposal to add a small per-endpoint burst pool on top of per-key token buckets. idea is: keep per-key steady-rate, but allow short bursts for chat/embeddings/rerank with different accounting.

sam: sounds useful. TL;DR: how big are we talking and where does streaming fit?

maria: sizes configurable by org tier + heuristic from recent 7d p50/p95 token spikes. streaming is different — it's event-rate (connections/sec) + token-rate. we should treat streaming bursts as connection quickstarts not token-firehoses.

raj: agree on different modes. for embeddings/rerank we charge per-vector/op, so burst buckets should be op-count based, not token-based. keep token-buckets for chat.

ellen: UX ask: Console should show 3 things per-route: current steady limit, burst capacity left, and a decomposition chart (tokens by origin: prefix, completion, tool-calls). also add a small "simulate burst" needle for cost estimations.

maria: exactly. we also need enforcement semantics: sliding-window + token-bucket hybird. allow short bursts until burst-pool drained, then fall back to steady-rate with 429 + Retry-After.

sam: implementation note: prefer keeping bursts as a separate counter + TTL keys in redis so eviction is easy. can have a shared org-level burst pool + siloed per-endpoint reserve. fallback policy: endpoint reserve -> org pool -> deny.

raj: what about model-fallback? e.g., if gpt-x chat hits burst, route to smaller quantized instance with degraded latency but allowed throughput. worth adding to routing policy.

maria: yes, routing policies should be able to declare compatible fallbacks. add metadata: "compatible_models": [] and a cost multiplier.

dev-bot: deploy check: there are 2 failing tests in quota-service CI related to burst TTL sharding. See: https://ci.internal/1234

ellen: telemetry: we need new series: burst_consumed_{endpoint,org}, burst_refill_events, burst_denied_count, and a histogram for denied_wait_seconds. pipe them into Console so SRE can set alerts.

ops-bot: alert: last night we saw a 20s tail on queue length for /chat-stream during a promo. drifted steady bucket but org burst exhausted.

sam: good example. this is why a small warm-up reserve per-org (not stealable for X seconds after allocation) would reduce noisy neighbor pain. suggestion: reserve 5% of monthly commit as non-stealable burst for tiered customers.

raj: API design detail: Add optional query params in token introspect: `?mode=burst` to see burst budget. For privacy, only return high-level numbers to user keys.

maria: error payloads should include: `code: rate_limit`, `scope: endpoint|org|key`, `remaining_burst_seconds`, `retry_after`. also include `suggested_fallback_model` when routing can degrade gracefully.

ellen: UX: on rollout page show per-org projected spend if they increase burst budget by X. add a checkbox in billing to opt-in to auto-burst-replenish (with caps).

sam: dev tasks: (1) quota-service: add burst pool counters + RBAC for config (2) router: implement fallback chain + compatible model metadata (3) console: display burst metrics and a simulate button (4) telemetry: new metrics + dashboards + alerts.

maria: I'll open a proposal PR with config schema. rough draft coming in ~2 hours. tagging @sam @ellen for review.

raj: ack, will review. also let's add a small internal experiment: try per-endpoint exponential backoff before 429 for 1 week. measure error surface.

ellen: one more: streaming SDKs should expose `onRetry` hook with a reason so clients can decide to buffer.

maria: noted. action items in thread: maria -> PR, sam -> quota-service sketch, ellen -> console mockups, raj -> routing fallback matrix. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
